title: The Attribution Contract for Generative Language Models
abstract: arXiv:2605.23080v3 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: Feature attribution scores each part of an input by how much it explains a model's output. We argue that in generative language models these scores carry no fixed meaning. A classifier has a single output to explain, but a generative model produces its output token by token, and each generated token is both an output and an input, so explaining the output becomes several distinct questions. We support this claim by proposing the Attribution Contract, a framework that names the question a set of attribution scores answers. A contract specifies the model score being explained, what is held fixed, the target output, the generation process, and which features can receive attribution, choices that matter in practice. For example, eligible features decide what a score explains: under a local next-token contract, the model's own generated tokens receive $29\%$ of the attribution mass, comparable to the $25\%$ on the input question, and read

translated_title: 生成式语言模型的归因契约
translated_abstract: 特征归因通过衡量输入的每个部分对模型输出的解释程度来为其打分。我们认为，在生成式语言模型中，这些分数没有固定的含义。分类器只有一个输出需要解释，而生成模型是逐个token生成输出的，每个生成的token既是输出又是输入，因此解释输出变成了几个不同的问题。我们通过提出“归因契约”这一框架来支持这一观点，该框架命名了一组归因分数所回答的问题。契约指定了被解释的模型分数、什么被固定、目标输出、生成过程以及哪些特征可以接受归因，这些选择在实践中至关重要。例如，合格特征决定了分数解释的内容：在局部下一token契约下，模型自身生成的token获得29%的归因权重，与输入问题上的25%相当，而读取...
tldr: 本文提出“归因契约”框架，指出生成式语言模型中归因分数没有固定含义，需明确契约条款（如目标输出和合格特征）才能赋予分数意义。
en_tdlr: This paper introduces the "Attribution Contract" framework, arguing that attribution scores in generative language models lack fixed meaning and require explicit contract terms (e.g., target output and eligible features) to give them significance.
